subject: Operational snapshot & customer bridge — LedgerWorks SEV outreach
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: ops@ledgerworks.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial notice: degraded inference performance affecting LedgerWorks (possible SEV-1)

Hi Daniel / LedgerWorks team,

We're seeing sustained latency and increased error rates impacting your realtime inference routes (route: ledger-embed-prod) starting ~08:45 PDT. We're treating this as an active incident and have opened a dedicated bridge.

What we know so far:
- Scope: ~12% of requests experiencing 5-10x latency spikes and occasional 503s across us-west-2 serving nodes.
- Impact: Customer-facing API calls that rely on fast embed+rerank are intermittently timing out.
- Initial mitigation: Traffic has been routed away from two suspect nodes; autoscaler triggered to add capacity.

Immediate asks:
1) Can your team confirm whether you've observed downstream client errors in the past 30 minutes?
2) Please join our bridge for a short sync at 09:30 PDT: meet.redwood.com/ledgerworks-bridge (will send invite).

We're prioritizing a fast, transparent update cadence. I will share a 30-minute snapshot and an exec-friendly summary after the first bridge.

Attachments: bridge-snapshot-20270607.txt (logs excerpt)

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: michael.grant@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial notice: degraded inference performance affecting LedgerWorks (possible SEV-1)

On Mon, 07 Jun 2027 at 09:12 AM, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> We're seeing sustained latency and increased error rates impacting your realtime inference routes...

Joined the bridge. Quick notes from ops:
- Root cause candidate: KV cache thrashing after an optimizer rollout to a repacked quantized variant last night. Several hosts are falling back to slower fp16 paths under load.
- Work in flight: rolling back the optimizer change on the two nodes showing highest miss rates. If rollback is successful, we expect tail latencies to normalize in 10-20 minutes.
- Customer-facing mitigation: enable prefix cache at the router layer for ledger-embed-prod to reduce repeated decode work.

I'll draft a short executive-facing statement for Daniel and their leadership right after we have the rollback confirmation.

-Marissa
Director, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: ops@ledgerworks.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, michael.grant@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Bridge update (10:05 PDT): mitigation underway, limited blast radius

Hi Daniel and LedgerWorks leadership,

Bridge summary (concise, exec-friendly):
- Incident: transient performance regression affecting LedgerWorks realtime inference traffic.
- Status: mitigation in progress. We initiated a targeted rollback of the quantized optimizer on two unhealthy hosts and enabled prefix-level caching at the router to reduce repeated work.
- Customer impact: ~8% of requests still experiencing elevated latency; overall request success rate has improved to 96%. No data loss.
- ETA: continuing monitoring; we expect stabilized latency within 30-45 minutes if rollback proceeds as planned.

Next steps for Redwood:
- Complete rollback and validate tail latency metrics.
- Perform a controlled warmup of KV caches for affected model variants.
- Produce an internal timeline and a preliminary postmortem within 48 hours.

Action items for LedgerWorks (if applicable):
- Optional: push non-critical background jobs to a later window if you see any elevated errors during the next hour.
- Please escalate any customer-facing incidents on your side to me directly so I can coordinate with our incident command.

We're attaching a short logs excerpt for your SREs. I'll follow with an exec note once we confirm the rollback.

Attachments: bridge-snapshot-20270607.txt

Best,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ops@ledgerworks.com
Cc: michael.grant@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridge update (10:05 PDT): mitigation underway, limited blast radius

On Mon, 07 Jun 2027 at 10:05 AM, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Bridge summary (concise, exec-friendly):
> - Incident: transient performance regression...

Rollback completed at 10:50 PDT. Observations:
- Tail latency returned to baseline (~p95 down from 2.3s to 140ms) on the previously affected hosts by 11:05 PDT.
- KV cache warmup: prefix cache reduced tokenization/decoding CPU pressure by ~35% after 20 minutes.
- Monitoring: no new 503 spikes in the last 20 minutes.

Containment confirmed. We're leaving the bridge open for verification for another hour and will publish a short postmortem with the timeline, technical RCA, and preventative actions by EOD tomorrow.

Planned follow-ups:
1) Postmortem draft and planned change window to properly roll the optimizer variant back to a canary with additional mem-pressure safeguards.
2) Add an automated health-check that will detect similar cache thrash patterns and surface before tail latency increases.

-Hannah
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: ops@ledgerworks.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, michael.grant@redwood.com, ceo@ledgerworks.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary & next steps (final) — LedgerWorks incident 2027-06-07

Daniel and leadership,

Final executive snapshot:
- What happened: a performance regression was introduced during a model optimizer rollout to a quantized variant. Under load this produced cache thrash on a subset of hosts, leading to elevated tail latency and intermittent 503s for LedgerWorks' realtime endpoints.
- Impact: Service degradation affecting ~8-12% of realtime calls over a ~90 minute window. No customer data was lost or corrupted.
- Action taken: immediate targeted rollback of the optimizer change, enabled prefix caching at the router, scaled additional healthy hosts, and monitored for regressions.
- Current state: service restored to baseline; no ongoing customer-facing errors as of 15:30 PDT.
- Timeline & deliverables:
  • Incident containment: 10:50 PDT (rollback completed).
  • Postmortem: Draft to be delivered to your team by 2027-06-08 EOD.
  • Preventative work: we will schedule a coordinated canary with additional mem-pressure safeguards and automated health checks. Goal: reduce recurrence risk and improve early detection.

Next steps for Redwood (owners):
- Marissa Cole: lead RCA and safety gate for optimizer rollouts. Target: postmortem + mitigation plan.
- Hannah Schmitt: implement cache-thrash monitor + run canary validation. Target: 3 weeks.
- Michael Grant: coordinate any billing/credits conversations if you saw customer impact; I will connect separately.

If you'd like a short executive call to review the timeline and remediation plan, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow morning. Thank you for your patience — we know reliability is non-negotiable and take this seriously.

Attachments: mitigation-checklist-20270607.pdf

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
